list-try-acrylic-pouring.description: This experimental painting features swirls of black, grey, purple, and white paints. As the paints began to dry, I took this closeup. The technique I use to create this kind of paint texture is called “fluid art,” and it relies on mixing a variety of mediums into acrylic paints to influence how they interact. I’ll use materials like glue, isopropyl alcohol, liquid silicone, and a butane torch.

list-watch-the-deer-rut.author: Andy Morffew from Itchen Abbas, Hampshire, UK
list-watch-the-deer-rut.description: When red deer stags rut, the second stage is that they display their antlers warning their opponent. If neither walks away, they start walking in parallel again.

list-watch-the-deer-rut.author: Andy Morffew from Itchen Abbas, Hampshire, UK
list-watch-the-deer-rut.description: Finally the red deer stags lock their antlers with great force and push with all their strength. Here the bigger stag is in the water and after a few minutes it became clear he could not push as well from there. He backed off to a small island close by and the other stag sat where he was. The two stags stayed together for over an hour and then they walked away to fight another day.

list-watch-the-deer-rut.author: Andy Morffew from Itchen Abbas, Hampshire, UK
list-watch-the-deer-rut.description: When red deer stags rut, after lots of roaring, they first have a stage of walking in parallel. They walk up and down sizing each other up and deciding if they want to walk away.

According to www.hawkmountain.org, this formation is a mile-long boulder field, up to 40 feet deep, which was deposited 10,000-12,000 years ago (the end of the last ice age), when glaciers stopped 40-50 miles to the north of this location. A periglacial process cracked boulders from the ridgetop that gradually slid to their current position.

list-walk-among-the-redwoods.description: This US National Monument is located 12 miles (19 Km) north of San Francisco and was named after a very influential Scottish-American naturalist. The main attraction of Muir Woods are the coast redwood (Sequoia sempervirens) trees which provide a wonderful environment to walk through and an opportunity to commune with nature.

list-walk-among-the-redwoods.author: Matthew Dillon from Hollywood, CA, USA
list-walk-among-the-redwoods.description: Muir Woods National Monument is part of California’s Golden Gate National Recreation Area, north of San Francisco. It’s known for its towering old-growth redwood trees. Trails wind among the trees to Cathedral Grove and Bohemian Grove, and along Redwood Creek. The Ben Johnson and Dipsea trails climb a hillside for views of the treetops, the Pacific Ocean and Mount Tamalpais in adjacent Mount Tamal

On this line also runs the Glacier Express, but there you are locked behind panorama windows. If you want to have one's cake and eat it too, you can take a normal train with a special carriage. The line is only conditionally avalanche safe, and sometimes the operation is stopped

list-ride-the-glacier-express.author: Kecko
list-ride-the-glacier-express.description: Last weekend brought winter into the Swiss mountains. The train of the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn disappears into the galleries and tunnels before it reaches the top of the pass. The Calmot avalanche galleries between Tschamut-Selva and Oberalp Pass which are open in summer, were already sealed with wooden planks. This route is also travelled by the Glacier Express. Switzerland, Nov 7, 2017.

list-see-monument-valley.author: Mike McBey
list-see-monument-valley.description: Arguably one of the best ways to see Monument Valley on the Utah/Arizona border is by driving round the unsurfaced roads (on payment of a fee).

list-see-monument-valley.author: Mike McBey
list-see-monument-valley.description: There is an unpaved road that you can drive on, to see some of Monument Valley. The scenery is -of course- on a grand scale. If you would prefer someone else to do the driving, there are several groups that, for a fee, will take you round.

list-see-monument-valley.author: Mike McBey
list-see-monument-valley.description: The valley, so familiar from Western Movies is located on the Arizona–Utah border and is the property of the Navajo Nation. Unsurprisingly it's very popular with visitors, who can (for a small fee) drive round part of the valley in their cars. Alternately you can go on a off-road tour, driven by locals or do part of the valley on horseback. Here we see a horse ranch in the valley.

list-see-monument-valley.author: Mike McBey
list-see-monument-valley.description: There is an unpaved road that you can drive on, to see some of Monument Valley. The scenery is -of course- on a grand scale. the valley and surrounding area belong to the Navajo Nation and they provide guided tours. I opted to drive round myself (not on a tour) and found no serious difficulties. Most is like in the photo - compacted sand - but some parts need a little more attention.
